children: NVIDIA Q2: revenue $96.2B (+106% YoY), Data Center $89B, adj EPS $2.22. Q3 guide ~$108B (±2%). FY28 revenue growth ~70%, gross margin ~75%. Notes memory and TSMC supply limits; $99B buyback left.
NVIDIA to buy Hugging Face for about $12.9B. Deal gives NVIDIA access to Hugging Face models, software and datasets, aiding integration with NVIDIA’s DGX Cloud and AI deployment.
NVIDIA and AWS will build US gov AI factories using 100,000 GPUs. NVIDIA NeMo models added to Bedrock/SageMaker. AWS to use NVIDIA Vera CPUs and NVLink Fusion integrations.
NVIDIA to backstop up to $105B for a Portsmouth, Ohio data‑center project and hold exclusive chip supply rights for the first half; total chip purchases for full deployment estimated at ~$350B.
NVIDIA (NVDA) paused parts of its revenue-sharing financing with AI cloud providers under two months after launch, halting some deals while it reviews and may revise or fold the program.
CEO Jensen Huang said NVIDIA demand now spans training, inference, enterprise computing, robotics and frontier AI. He affirmed OpenAI and Anthropic will remain long-term NVIDIA customers.
NVIDIA (NVDA) drove strong quarterly results with high data‑center revenue; SK Hynix plans a $4B HBM plant in Indiana to expand memory supply for AI systems used with NVIDIA, opening H2 2028.
Hark struck a multi‑year tie-up with NVIDIA (NVDA) to develop agentic, personalized AI using NVIDIA’s large-scale GPU compute. Hark says its initial AI platform will launch soon.
Analyst upgrades lifted NVIDIA (NVDA) price targets; Evercore raised its target to $465 from $413, citing the company's demand-supply management after recent results.
Mizuho maintained its Outperform rating on NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) and raised its price target for the stock to $315 from $300.
